cues: Ferenc Molnár was Hungary's most celebrated playwright, born in Budapest in eighteen seventy eight.
He studied law, became a journalist, and made his name with the novel The Paul Street Boys and plays like Liliom, later the musical Carousel.
Jewish, he left Europe in nineteen forty and died in New York.
He wrote witty, sophisticated drawing room comedies, and is often compared with Oscar Wilde and Bernard Shaw.
